# Vault release cadence

@include 'alerts/enterprise-only.mdx'

Vault Enterprise and HCP Vault Dedicated 2.x and later follow the release
cadence and fix policy described on this page. Vault 1.x releases retain their
existing maintenance terms. For HCP Vault Dedicated, version availability and
upgrade timing follow the service's
[version management guidance](/vault/cloud/versions).

## Vault versioning

@include 'version-syntax.mdx'

## Feature release windows

Vault plans four feature release windows each year: an annual major release in
May and minor releases in February, August, and November. The annual major
release cadence begins with Vault 3.0 in May 2027. These windows are planning
targets and may change. Refer to the
[release notes](/vault/docs/updates/release-notes) for available releases.

## Feature and fix availability

New features go into the latest minor of the current major. Features are not
backported to earlier minors or older majors.

Bug and security fixes go into the latest minor of each major that remains
eligible for fixes. For example, when 2.2 becomes available, upgrade from 2.1
to 2.2 and apply its latest patch to receive subsequent fixes.

When a minor stops receiving fixes, subsequent fixes become available in the
newer minor within that major. The end of new fixes for a minor differs from
the end of technical support. You may still have access to Support under your
terms, but resolving an issue may require upgrading to a release that contains
the fix.

## Final minor releases

The **final minor** is the last minor released within a major version.
Intermediate minors are superseded by newer minors in the same major, which
become the destination for subsequent fixes. Because no later minor replaces
the final minor, it continues to receive eligible fixes under the major's
remaining support lifecycle after feature development moves to the next major.

When 3.0 becomes available, new features move to 3.x, while the final 2.x minor
remains the destination for eligible 2.x fixes. A final minor does not start a
new support period or receive a new long-term support designation. The support
lifecycle begins with the major release, and minor and patch releases do not
restart it. Fix availability depends on the major's support phase. Sustained
Support does not include new bug or security fixes.

The following example shows how fixes move to each newer minor within a major,
while the final minor continues receiving eligible patches after the next
major becomes available. The longer patch lines show the final minor of each
major.

![Illustrative release timeline showing release branches and patch sequences, with 2.3.x, 3.3.x, and 4.3.x shown as the final minors of their respective majors.](/img/release-cadence-vault-docs_light.png#light-theme-only)
![Illustrative release timeline showing release branches and patch sequences, with 2.3.x, 3.3.x, and 4.3.x shown as the final minors of their respective majors.](/img/release-cadence-vault-docs_dark.png#dark-theme-only)

The timeline illustrates the release pattern. Its patch counts and endpoints
do not promise a fixed number of patches or establish support deadlines. Refer
to [Vault Enterprise support](/vault/docs/enterprise/support) for support phase
coverage. Use the
[IBM Software Support Lifecycle](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/lifecycle/)
for authoritative Base, Extended, and Sustained Support dates. Search for
HashiCorp Vault and select the applicable Vault Self-Managed lifecycle record.
Do not infer an end-of-support date from a minor release date.

## Patch availability

Patches target a monthly cadence for releases eligible for fixes. The monthly
cadence is a planning target, not a guarantee that every eligible minor has a
release each month. Use the release notes to confirm available fixes. Refer to
applicable security advisories or Support guidance for information about a
specific issue.

## Upgrade planning

While your major is receiving new minors, move to its latest minor to receive
subsequent fixes. After you move to its final minor, you can remain on that
minor while it remains eligible for fixes, keeping its patches current.

You can remain on an older major after a newer major becomes available when
the older major remains eligible for fixes and you run its final minor with
current patches. Features introduced in a newer major require upgrading to a
release that contains them.

The final minor can support a longer interval between feature upgrades, but
your plan must account for its availability and remaining fix coverage. Do not
wait for a future release when doing so creates a coverage gap. You may need an
interim upgrade, and you should continue applying eligible patches between
feature upgrades.

The release policy does not define supported upgrade paths. Check the source
and target versions in the [upgrade guide](/vault/docs/upgrade), including any
required intermediate versions. Review your deployment topology and test the
upgrade before changing production environments.
